[Figure 1]

In the figure shown, line $m$ is parallel to line $n$, and line $k$ intersects both lines. What is the value of $w$?
explanation: Choice B is correct. When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, corresponding angles are equal. In the figure, line $m$ is parallel to line $n$, and both are intersected by transversal line $k$. The angle measuring $125\degree$ is formed between line $k$ and line $m$ on one side of the transversal. The angle $w$ is formed between line $k$ and line $n$ in the corresponding position (same side of the transversal, same relative position). By the corresponding angles theorem, these angles are equal. Therefore, $w = 125\degree$. Note that the $55\degree$ angle shown at line $m$ and the $125\degree$ angle form a linear pair (supplementary angles on a straight line), which can be verified: $125 + 55 = 180\degree$.
